title: Like a dream and a show
hook: know this world like a dream and a show; none of it is true without the Lord (Salok M9, ang 1427)

segments.voice: Yesterday, fear none: frighten no one, and take fear from no one. What makes that kind of courage possible? Part of the answer is in today's salok.

You're in a dream, and it's urgent. You've missed the exam, or the train is leaving, or you're back at an old school and can't find the classroom. Your heart is pounding. It's completely real. Then your eyes open. The ceiling. The alarm clock. Your own bed. In about three seconds the whole drama drains away, and you almost laugh. Guru Tegh Bahadur's salok asks what it would be like to see the whole world with those first waking eyes.
screen: `THE DREAM: URGENT AND REAL.` → `EYES OPEN: THE CEILING.` → `WAKING EYES.`

segments.voice: The salok says jio supnaa ar pekhnaa, aise jag kau jaan. In paraphrase: like a dream and a show, know the world to be so. In all of it, nothing is saacho, true, says Nanak, except the Lord. Supnaa is a dream. Pekhnaa is a show, a spectacle, the kind of street play or puppet performance a crowd gathers to watch. It's vivid, it pulls you in, you might even cry. Then the curtain drops and everyone goes home. This salok needs to be heard alongside the rest of the Granth. In Sukhmani, Guru Arjan says the Lord is true, and everything He has made is true. So Sikh teaching doesn't call the world a lie in the sense of fake. Both lines are in the same scripture, and Sikh teachers hold them together: the world is real as the Lord's creation, and passing as a dream is passing. Read beside Sukhmani, saacho here points to what lasts. What isn't true is our grip on the world, taking the show for the whole of reality. Now go back to yesterday's courage. Sikhs remember Guru Tegh Bahadur facing the empire's threats in Delhi without fear, and some readers hear this salok as part of the reason: he saw those threats with waking eyes. Real, and terrible, but not the thing that lasts. The dream isn't worthless. It just isn't the place to build your whole life. Wake up inside it, and you can play your part in the show without forgetting it's a show.
screen: `SUPNAA: A DREAM.` · `PEKHNAA: A SHOW ON A STREET.` · `TRUE AS HIS, PASSING AS A DREAM.` · `WAKING EYES, EVEN IN DANGER.` · then, large: `LIKE A DREAM.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and recall any dream, last night's or any vivid one, even a fragment, and notice how real it felt and how quickly it faded on waking. Then open your eyes and look around the room with the same fresh, waking eyes: the chair, the light, your hands, real and passing. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru between breaths, the One the salok says remains.
Supnaa, a dream. The salok asks us to know the world like supnaa, and pekhnaa, a show: vivid, real while it lasts, and passing, while the Lord remains.
Your line: like a dream. Waking eyes can still love the show. That's day five hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear this salok at the close of every complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib; teachers often read it beside Guru Arjan's line that the Lord is true and all He made is true, so that the world is honored and held lightly at once.

original.note: Gurmukhi: supnaa, a dream. The salok pairs it with pekhnaa, a show.

trapdoor: what you thought: like a dream means the world doesn't matter.
what it means: the world is the Lord's real creation, but it passes; don't take the show for the whole of reality.

what a scholar hears: the Granth holds both 'all He made is true' in Sukhmani and 'like a dream and a show' in the ninth Guru's saloks, and Sikh commentators read them together rather than choosing one.

chat.says: If the world is like a dream, does that mean none of it is real?
options: It's real as the Lord's creation, but passing like a dream; only the Lord lasts.
Yes; the salok says nothing matters, so you don't have to care how you act.
No; it means only our dreams at night are unreal, and waking life lasts forever.
chat.meaning: Jio supnaa ar pekhnaa: like a dream and a show. Beside Sukhmani, the world is real as His creation, yet passing; only the Lord remains.

Sukhmani.meaning: Guru Arjan's long hymn of peace
